svg.title: Takeoff angle, skip zone and NVIS
svg.desc: Not to scale. A station on the left sends signals into the ionosphere at different angles. A wave sent too steeply, above the critical angle, passes through the ionosphere and is lost. A wave at a lower angle is refracted back to Earth far away. Between the end of the ground wave and the point where the sky wave first comes down is the skip zone, where normally nothing is heard; weak scatter signals can sometimes reach it. On a lower frequency, below the critical frequency, even a wave sent almost straight up comes back down near the station: near vertical incidence skywave (NVIS), which covers short distances with no skip zone.
